utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, this is Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Krsnik: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you remember, last time we broke when we were looking at the photograph of Heliodrom. And I would like to round this off, Heliodrom again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the record, and possibly to gain a complete picture, let us go back to this Exhibit 20.8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, all I want to ask you: If you would be so kind as to make a circle and also describe verbally what you told us already last time, who was in which building. For instance, put "HV," and then put a letter "A," and put the HVO Brigade with a "B," and a "C" if there was a third party there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that in these three buildings, this one, this one, and this one. And the three units were quartered there, two units of the Croatian army, parts of the 1st and 2nd Guards Brigades, and one HVO unit from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which building and which -- and the 1st and 2nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please put the 1st Brigade -- let's use letter "A." This is all in the record, Witness. Put "B" where the 2nd Brigade was, you say, the 2nd Guard Brigade with letter "B." And "C," let's make it the HVO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "B" is the 2nd Guard Brigade, and "C" is the HVO unit from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very good. Now, when you say "parts," what were these called, companies of these brigades? What were they? How many men could it be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is hard for me to say, because I could not see them line up to establish the exact count and their exact strength. But I -- my guess is that in the area of Mostar --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just a moment. I'm asking you about Heliodrom. I assume that you cannot know what the situation in Mostar is, since you were at the Heliodrom, and that is why I am asking you about Heliodrom. How many men from these guards brigades could there be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess between 150 to 200 soldiers, because I used to see, say, groups of 30 and more in one place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell us: With all the insignia of the Croatian army, or without them, when you said that you guessed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. They had Croatian army insignia on their clothes, and the vehicles they used had the markings of the Croat Defence Council. They had removed their plates from these vehicles and put on the plates of the Croat Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, sir. I'm sorry I'm interrupting you, but I would like this cross-examination to make faster, more specific. Did you see them remove the plates and put on new plates? And just take it easy, please. Let us not overlap. What we want to know is what you eyewitnessed. If you heard something, please tell us, "I heard this and that." If you saw something, then tell us again, sir, because after all, we are before an august Chamber, so we need to know that. So you did not see them change the plates, did you? It is your assumption, or did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're not allowing me to finish my sentence. I know where I am as well as you do. I didn't see them change the plates, but I know very precisely that those men came from a unit of the Croatian army and they were driving vehicles marked with the markings of the Croat Defence Council. On the doors, they had -- they had stuck the marks of the Croat Defence Council. And I was driven in such a vehicle itself, and I know that those units belong to the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will allow you to finish every sentence that you want. I want merely to agree with you very nicely. And you did not tell me whether you saw it personally, or did you hear about it, or is it that you assumed that. Because when you see the plates, they are just the HVO plates, isn't it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was asking you a very simple question. You don't have to get angry with me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not angry with you at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I just want to remind you, speak very slowly and make a pause between questions and answers. The interpreters are really having a very difficult time to follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honours. I will bear it in mind. But, you know, it is very hard indeed, because I interrupt the witness and then I am told why don't I let him go on? And if the witness gets diverted then -- and I wanted to cut this cross-examination short. And in that case, overlappings are inevitable, because we speak the same language. So if you do not get the interpretation the very moment when we have said something, I'm very sorry. But I will bear this in mind. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I believe this statement you made just now is fast enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did this, as you say, HV, have any tanks? Its tanks, I mean.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that. I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any artillery? I mean heavy guns, howitzers, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If mortars are 120 millimetres or 82 millimetres, which I see, if they are heavy artillery, then, yes, they did have them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And other heavy pieces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many trucks did they have, if you can tell us that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I did not count them. But between these buildings and in front of these buildings which I marked, their vehicles were parked there. Those were vehicles used by the Yugoslav People's Army, and we called them -- and I served in that army myself. We called them 110s -- or rather, I think -- I think that the proper name was T-110. And they mostly served for lighter artillery pieces in the former army, and those vehicles were the ones that they used most often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these vehicles were at the Heliodrom? They did not arrive in them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them in front of the building in which these units were quartered. I saw them use them. And I said that I was also driven in one of such vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand, Witness. You don't think that I'm not following what you are saying. I am asking you: Do you know if they arrived in those cars and were those vehicles belonging to the former army were at the Heliodrom, why do you claim that those were their vehicles? I mean, if you know it, you know it. If you don't, you don't. You don't have to answer every one of my questions. If you don't, just tell me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But you are changing the subject. I'm not the one who was supervising the buildings or the Heliodrom. I was a prisoner there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And at some point, I learned that there was the Croatian army there. At some point, they took me over there to clean their premises, and I see cars which they use, and they tell me they are professional Croatian troops and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, excuse me. I have to interrupt you. And I am sorry I have to do that, but my question is -- I'm asking you one thing, and you immediately move on to different tracks and give me a different answer. My simple question was: Do you know whose trucks these are? And nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I do not believe that's so. You were asking him very detailed questions, and he was explaining that he was a prisoner, not a supervisor, but that he was telling you what he saw, and then you interrupted him. So you have to be a little bit more fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour. Maybe there is a misunderstanding, because when I hear a claim and I ask about these trucks, they are the HVO, and then when I ask the witness, he proceeds with his own story. And my simple question is: Does he know, has he heard, or is he making assumptions as to who these trucks belong to? If he doesn't know it, he doesn't know it. He doesn't have to know everything. But never mind. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let us move away from Heliodrom and go to another topic. Tell me, who was the first one who took you to Rastani and why? Which date was it, which month? I see that you remember dates very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first time I was taken to Rastani, on a Sunday, the 5th of September. And I stayed there seven days until the next Sunday, the 12th of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my chief question was: Who took you there, which unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was some men who came from the 2nd Battalion. They took us to a place called Rudnik, that is, the northern part of Mostar. And from there, we walked to the village of Rastani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which brigade it was, but the 2nd HVO Battalion. Those were mostly people from Rudnik, I think. Even the headquarters was in the part of Mostar called Rudnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in whose hands was Rastani at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO's hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the BH army take Rastani for the first time? What month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. All I know is that Rastani was -- changed hands several times. But when it happened the first time, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So that was the 5th of September. You go back. And is it then that the BH army attacks and takes Rastani over following that 5th of September? Perhaps you know the date or something.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the BH army entered Rastani on the 19th of September, on Sunday, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why is -- why do you still have this 19th of September, precisely the 19th, in your memory? Why did it stuck in your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it did because I was in the camp that day for the -- for another two or three days. And all men incarcerated at the Heliodrom were denied food and all the rest. That is what the guards formally allowed them to do, to avail them of any facilities. And the explanation was that Rastani had fallen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Somebody explained it to you that that was why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody explained it to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if nobody explained it to you, then how do you know that it was the 19th if you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because on the 20th, I was taken to prepare the action for the recapture of Rastani so that I was in contact with people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you learned about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, please, who is it that you learned about it from? Who told you about all this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is difficult for me to remember now who it was that told me that, because I didn't even know the names of those people. But on the 21st, in the afternoon - and that was Tuesday - when I was taken to the village of Djubrani - and I explained it already in my statement - that whole day, that is, Wednesday, the 22nd of September, I spent that whole day with several soldiers fortifying the positions. I mean, I spent the whole day with them and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now tell me, what battalion did they come from? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What battalion they came from? I think I cannot really affirm that with any certainty, but I think that those men with whom we worked up there, around those positions on the 22nd, I think those were artillery men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were under whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please -- I am just being warned - my colleague is - that the record doesn't reflect my question and your answer. Do you remember my question? Did you learn at the Heliodrom about the fall of Rastani? Do you remember your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 19th to the 20th. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following question is frequently asked here: Did you learn later on which units it involved? What was that action of the BH army which took Rastani on the 21st? What units were engaged in that, and what kind of operation was it? What was it's scale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know. I did not learn that. But between the 5th and the 12th of September, while I was in Rastani, they were also --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you that, Witness. My question was very simple, and that was whether you learned it. You say "I didn't," then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's it. And did you learn later on or at that time, talking to soldiers when you were with them -- because I see that you have -- that you communicate very broadly. Was it a large-scale operation involving Zuka's unit, Black Swans, that there was a major pogrom, major destruction, sabotage units were infiltrated behind the back of the HVO in Mostar suburbs, and so on and so forth? Did you learn about that afterwards, or perhaps then, from those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell me: On the 21st of September, who takes you, you said, to the -- to a place called Djubrani? Who takes you there, to whom he takes you, why does he take you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I was taken from the camp every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine, fine. But I'm asking about the 21st.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But do you think that I had a possibility or any right to ask them "Where are you taking me and why"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely. I don't think you could --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then how can you think that I could find out that night where they were taking me? Had I known who was taking me -- if I knew who had taken me, I would have told you. But those men who took me treated us correctly; I mean the ten of us who were taken that day. But who they were, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, Witness. I'm not trying to upset you. I do not place you in discomfiture in any way whatsoever. I'm asking you because you so far told us, "I went to this and this battalion. I worked with this and that." So far you have always told us with whom you worked and for whom you worked. This is the first time you are telling us you don't know. And it is all right with me. I mean, you just don't know. But be that as it may, somebody came to the Heliodrom to fetch you and took you away, and the military police recorded that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were brought back on the 23rd, the military police again recorded that, who brought you there and how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you cannot tell me who it was that you worked there for or why? I mean on the 21st, 22nd.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we were fortifying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do not know for whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, fine. That's okay. Tell me, please, apart from that gun which you told us you had to charge, did you see any artillery at that place with your own eyes, or did you only hear it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that place where I charged that gun?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean artillery generally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Artillery, according to you, of the HVO, which fired at Rastani. According to you, did you see it with your own eyes? I know that one gun which you charged, of course you saw that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this day the artillery was active all day, heavy artillery pieces beyond the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. I couldn't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, there is no need to create some tension between the two of us. I'm asking you nicely, and you can answer me briefly and nicely.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's you who thinks I'm creating tension.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm not trying to engage in any discussion with you. I'm merely trying to avoid situations which can produce some discussions, so I'm asking you nicely. And I can see that you are an intelligent and learned man, so you can give me short answers. Tell me, please, did you -- the gentleman that you called Tuta, did you see him anywhere except at Djubrani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, tell me, please, this emblem which was on the sleeve, you told us, on the left sleeve, this emblem of the Convicts Battalion --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you first: You remember the statement that you gave to the investigators of the Tribunal, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you remember that you described at great length and in every detail that emblem and then drew also a picture of it to substantiate your description. Tell us, how many statements have you given to this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To The Hague investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give any to the AID, to the military, to the security service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And how did The Hague investigators find you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wondered about that myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, you wondered about that yourself. And on the basis of this emblem, you recognised, and to this day you claim, that those who wore those emblems on the sleeve were members of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to answer your questions with only yes or no?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we shall not be able to arrive at the truth, and you said that that was the -- our purpose, and I think that is our purpose. It does not say anywhere that this was the emblem by which I recognised that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I will now stop you. Take your statement -- oh, you don't have the statement in front of you. Well, I'll give you a copy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just say one sentence, please? It does not say anywhere here that it was that emblem on the basis of which I identified that unit. I identified the unit, I recognised that unit on the basis of the following: In the evening of the 22nd --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to that later. I first want to clear up these things about the emblem. Everything is all right. No problem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do finish, because the Chamber thinks that you should finish your sentence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the evening of the 22nd, a group of soldiers told me that Tuta's men had arrived. I saw them in the afternoon, but I did not know who they -- what they were. The next day, around 12.00, I saw Tuta lead a group of men personally. In the afternoon, I saw a soldier ask his commander to tell Tuta that he is sick and that he can not participate in combat. All this proves that it was that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, but I cannot conduct my cross-examination in this manner. Your Honour, Judge Clark, whatever you wish. I'm trying to clarify. I ask one thing, and the witness always answers something else, what he wants to say, not what I'm asking him about, although I don't object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Krsnik, you have a statement. The witness has a statement. And you're jumping from his previous testimony the other day to what he said in the statement. We don't have a statement. And I'm a little lost at what's going on, but I think that the witness is trying to clarify something, and you're too far ahead of him. Maybe if you both slow down a little bit. You both have -- whatever part of the country you come from, you both speak extremely fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have heard what the Trial Chamber has said, and please, answer my questions. Let me explain to you. It is my right to put questions to you and to ask you to answer with yes or no. It is a right I have according to the Statute of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, there are many questions to which the answer yes or no is neither accurate nor fair. And I think, you know some answers are yes or no and some answers require elucidation. So Witness, you can answer both ways, and we will tell you how you are to do it, not Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. I only wanted to bring this part of the examination to a close and to arrive at an explanation, because the witness wasn't answering my questions as I asked them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave a statement to the investigators of this Tribunal in 1998, and on page 9 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask the usher --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you right away: Why have you never said until today, either in your statement or to the question put to you by the Prosecution, that it was from others you heard that Tuta's army was coming, Tuta's soldiers were coming? Because that is not to be found anywhere in your statement. Look at the last two pages -- last two sentences on page 8: "The attack" -- that's page 8, the last two sentences. "The attack was conducted by a unit called the Convicts Battalion." You claim that's Tuta's unit. "I saw the insignia. I saw Tuta himself. I made a drawing of the insignia of that unit. The insignia was on the left sleeve. The background of the insignia was black. The lightning was yellow. And the letters Kaznjenicka Bojna were, I think, in white." And Kaznjenicka Bojna is in quotation marks. "On the right sleeve, the soldiers had the normal HVO insignia." You see, in your statement, you say that it was the Convicts Battalion that launched the attack and that you recognised them. And there is no other explanation here in your statement, and not until today have you given any other explanation except that you recognised them by their insignia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct? Is this what you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this statement well, and that's what I stated at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, please, when and at what point did an ambulance arrive, as you described yesterday when answering my learned friend's questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What ambulance are you referring to? Because ambulances arrived on two occasions. Was it the ambulance I was taken away in?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't understand that there were two incidents involving an ambulance, I have to say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One ambulance arrived early on and took away a group of eight men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An ambulance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And on the second occasion, an ambulance came to get me and my colleague. That was at around 10.00 or just after 10.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because, as you said, a shell landed at that time, which wounded the doctor, and this is not mentioned in your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. That was on the 22nd. That was on the 22nd of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, please listen carefully to my questions. I asked you when and where. If it was on the 22nd, well, then it was on the 22nd. So I want to know when the shell landed and which doctor it wounded.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I thought you were asking me about the ambulance that took me to Rastani. But --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you see, this is something I'm hearing for the third time now, that you were taken to Rastani, but it doesn't say so in your statement. It says you were taken to a village 2 and-a-half or 3 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's in the direction of Rastani, going from Djubrani towards Rastani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I think he gave this evidence the other day, because I recall the story about the argument between two ambulance drivers as to who would go down. One was faster; one was slower. And then they had the wounded soldier. I think it's better if you concentrate on what he said in his oral testimony than rather, because we're getting confused. You're jumping. If I'm getting confused up here where there's no tension, it must be very, very difficult for the witness. I recall evidence about two ambulances and an exchange of a wounded soldier, and then his going in the other ambulance, the slower ambulance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's clarify this, then. In your statement which you made to the investigators of this Tribunal, you do not mention anywhere the incident of a shell landing and wounding a doctor. This is something you mentioned for the first time before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are details. Things like that happened every minute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When this shell landed, who were the soldiers guarding? Who was in charge of you throughout those two or three days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was a soldier who I think was called Zdenko. And there was another soldier whose name was, I think, Mirko, and he was a building construction engineer. He had worked in Herzegovina up to the war. He guarded us in Djubrani and on that day, that is, the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were taken 2 and-a-half kilometres from Djubrani in the direction of Rastani in an ambulance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A soldier came -- well, first you came to the village, and then a soldier came who took you to bunker, if I remember well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did that soldier belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Tuta's unit. He came from the group, which was in that cluster of houses where Tuta took a group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that for certain, or are you simply assuming this? Please tell us honestly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot assert that with certainty. But on that day, the infantry operation, and at these positions from which shots were fired, it was only Tuta's unit that took part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean from that direction, or in general?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that axis, the bunker, the bend, the road, which I sketched yesterday, there were about 15 artillery pieces from which they were firing at the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us clarify first. Was it only Tuta's unit who took Rastani, or were there other units as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers were there, then, who were able to take or restore Rastani on their own? Rastani had been fortified, if I understand correctly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rastani was not fortified at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at the picture, and then we'll use that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yesterday, I think I said as far as I was able to see that day, an infantry attacked Rastani and there were about five groups of about ten soldiers each, so all in all about 50 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these 50 men took Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will explain that later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that Rastani was not fortified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I passed through that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Through the whole village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through -- from Dumporove Kuce to Elektroprenos, and then some 30 or 50 metres to the right, and then I went back for about 100 metres to the left, and nowhere did I see a single fortification or a single bunker. The soldiers who were there were in the first houses, but there were no fortifications or bunkers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. I will now show you a picture, and then we shall talk on the basis of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, can I ask you something? You're going into very fine detail about the capture, or the fall, or the recapture, of Rastani. What exactly is the point you're trying to make? Are you trying to say that this witness was not there or that your client's unit was not there? Or what point are you trying to make? Why are we going into all this detail and you're not actually putting to this witness what your client's case is, as you're bound to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with all due respect, I have learned a lot listening to you here, and I think that this has enriched my experience as a lawyer, but I see no reason why I should tell this witness about my cross-examination. I admit that this is the first time I am conducting cross-examination before this Tribunal. I have worked in America where cross-examination looks quite different. My task here, as counsel, Your Honour -- I have analysed this, and this is not the first witness from Rastani, and last night we analysed the statements of other witnesses. So please allow me to check this witness's testimony. And whether he is being honest or not is for you to determine, but we shall later compare the statements of witnesses. Because how would it be possible for several people to say quite different things about the same event? I hope my learned friends will not object to this. But I wish to check this. He says it was only the Convicts Battalion. I wish to check that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Normally in cross-examination - I think you know this, Mr. Krsnik - is that certainly you're entitled to check the credibility of the witness, but the next thing that you have to go on to say is that, "Mr. SS, you cannot be correct in this because my client will say, or my witnesses will say, or somebody will say that on that particular day, the Convicts Battalion was actually in action somewhere else 20 kilometres away." That's the sort of thing you've got to put. You're probing, probing, probing, but we are getting nowhere. We are wondering - you're going into such detail about the attack of Rastani - are we coming to a point? And then we just move on to something else. So cross-examination has to elicit something that's valuable to us as well, obviously, as to your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My client claims he -- or rather, the Convicts Battalion was 15 kilometres away from that spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Well, you see, Mr. Krsnik, that's really valuable. You must put it to this person, because we certainly are being kept in the dark about it. We are wondering why are you asking this witness such detailed questions without actually saying to him, "We don't believe you because X, Y and Z."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The men who wore this patch perhaps were in Rastani, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I will now show you a picture and ask you to tell us whether you see the houses in question on this picture, 34.3. Witness, look at this picture, please. Where are the houses called Dumporove Kuce, and where were the two prisoners that you found, you know, when two groups came across each other with a group of soldiers from the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dumporove Kuce are not visible on this picture at all. I assume it was taken from the air. This is a photograph taken looking in the direction of Rastani from the side controlled by the HVO. That's the way this picture was made. And Dumporove Kuce would be located somewhere around here, in this corner, in the very corner here. But they are not visible in the photograph. And there is a street leading from Dumporove Kuce here, and we took that road to here, which I think is Elektroprenos, and this is the part going in the direction of Mostar, where this grain elevator is, and this photograph was taken from the other side, compared to the map that we looked at yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us, where they brought the two prisoners, is that place visible on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's not visible either. I said yesterday in my statement that we came as far as Elektroprenos, turned a little to the right, 20 or 30 metres, then the commander of our group was given information that there were two prisoners, and then we retraced our steps and went to a place which is not visible on this photograph. It was about 100 or 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can't see it on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at page 11 of your statement. Start from the top where you say: "We arrived at the railway tracks."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "And we stopped in a house to take a rest."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Both groups of soldiers contacted Kolobara to tell him that they had taken prisoner two members of the army." Then I will skip to the sentence when he heard that the two men had been taken prisoner. Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kolobara said, "We're not going to the Neretva. We're going left so we can meet up with this group. When we met up with the other group, I think their leader's name was Zdenko ..." And my first question to you: Is that the same Zdenko who was guarding you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. "And two members of the army were lying down on the ground." Would you please show me the railway tracks on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it here. I cannot say on this photograph where it is, but I know for certain that that day and that evening, the groups of Tuta's unit only went as far as the railway tracks, only as far as the railway tracks, and not a single soldier crossed them. I think that the railway tracks are somewhere close by. And this is the main road on the other side of the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "Tuta's units," are you referring to the units of five or ten men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, say that, then, please, because everything has to be translated here. Witness, I have consulted my colleagues, and I, of course, have visited Rastani on several occasions. Is this not the railway track behind the grain elevator? You see there are some pylons there for the locomotive. Well, I'll give you another photograph where you can see it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask for Exhibit 34.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Can I just ask what the point of all this? Because I am really getting lost of what the point is, whether the railroad --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll explain. I'll explain it in no time at all. Your Honours, let me explain a bit to the Prosecutor and to the witness. I'm asking these questions because the witness, who was one of those arrested, and he made his statement and made the positions and said that it all happened, and so I'm trying to ask questions about the place where he was found. Do we need anything else, my learned friend or -- or rather, I have a suggestion, Your Honours. From tomorrow on, we were talking about this, to prepare a summary of our cross-examination and give the Prosecutor a day in advance, what we're going to ask and who it refers to and all that. Perhaps that might cut our time shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, nobody is asking you to do that, but usually cross-examination is based on what the witness said in court, and possibly, if it varies terribly from his statement, you can put the statement. But you seem to concentrate on what he said previously, rather than what he says in court. And we don't know what he said in the statement previously, and we're wondering why you spend so much time on the statement and not on his oral evidence. But is it suggested to this witness -- just to put my mind at ease, is it suggested to this witness that he wasn't there at all or that -- you know, why does it make any difference where the railway is if you say your client wasn't there at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps this witness did not see it being poured. Perhaps it's just hearsay. If the one on whom it was poured on, then he indicated the location exactly before this Court, and it is not the same location which the witness is pointing at this place. I mean, they are not the same. So everybody was in the camp. And let us now go back into detail about some other things. But we hear different stories, but it's all hearsay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the railway track on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, sir, these photographs are inversed. This photograph was taken more or less from the side controlled by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, more or less from Zelig [phoen]. So when you look at it, it has nothing to do with this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Can you see the railroad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see where the railroad is. You see where it is. So it is quite true that we reached the Elektroprenos, as I said. And in the immediate vicinity, you can see how many metres it is. At that time, I could not measure it, whether it's 20 or 50 metres, but the railroad is in the immediate vicinity of the Elektroprenos, that is, electrical transmitter line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a photograph that shows the exact distance between the Elektroprenos and the railroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we have Exhibit 20.7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you can see this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now you see the power transmission, and you see the railroad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perfect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you say, "We reached the railroad." Now, of course, I'm not going to speculate how far it is from the power transmission, but it's not far.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had come to one of these houses, one of these houses, and so all this is clear, this road, and so on and so forth, and we did not go further than the railroad that day, and we stopped in one of these houses here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I ask another question for clarification? Are these houses in this photograph now the Dumpor's houses? I think that's what my note says, "Dumpor houses."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far are these houses from Dumpor's houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You can take a map and measure it. One can measure it exactly on the map. At that time, I covered it on foot in a human shield, mixed --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. Wait, wait, wait, wait, wait. We'll come to that. That's another matter. So I see you always have excellent information at your disposal. Now, tell me, in your view, how far is it from Dumpor's houses, a kilometre, half a kilometre, 2 kilometres, 100 metres? You can tell us approximately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few hundred metres, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now tell me, please, will you describe to the Court how is it that you walked, that is, you moved towards those houses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell us how is it that you walked, you and the soldiers? That is, where did you come from? And will you please use the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We came -- I think we came from the -- we came down this road - or perhaps there is another road beyond this power transmission installation - and then turned right, because in Rastani, I was only on those occasions, so I cannot really say it with certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that you knew Rastani very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do, but I can't know it to a house, as you want me to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, how did you walk, you and the soldiers, towards these houses? And did they let you know from the hill where the BH army was or didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, only two minutes to explain what a human shield is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the first time in my life, I heard the term "human shield" in the summer of 1993. At that time -- until that time, I still didn't know what it meant. In the camp, I was told that on the Bulevar and on Santic Street, human shields were being used. And when I asked what is that, they told me, "Captured men are used in combat by putting them in front of the soldiers." And indeed, that was the practice. That was a widespread phenomenon in all the combat actions planned and carried out by the HVO, and in particular, this unit, the military police unit on Santic Street. To have a human shield, the following is needed: Number 1, you must have people deprived of all their rights. That is, you must have slaves. Because a man who has even the slightest right cannot be sent there. So such a man, deprived of all his rights, you use in combat. He participates directly in combat, and he becomes a live target, an undefended, live target that very moment. He may not take cover, take shelter, try to save himself, and he has nothing to defend himself with. I really did not believe -- could not believe that there existed such phantom minds which could allow themselves to do that in a war with a human beings at the end of the 20th Century. And that was a widespread phenomenon, a common phenomenon. I myself participated in such a human shield for days on end. And the counsel asks me about my testimony, if it is hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness SS, I have the right to ask you about things that you were present at, before the Court, as I asked you in the beginning, and very kindly, to tell us about your experience and about what you heard or what you guessed at, that you should indicate it. Now, this was a military theoretical explanation of the human shield that you studied, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not study it. I was prepared, you know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, what it looked like in Rastani, because you said that you were part of the human shield?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, now, you told the Court what it looked like at Rastani, to be a human shield there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was -- it looked -- it was as follows: When I arrived in Rastani, at Dumpor's houses, I found there a group of four captured men --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness -- Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no. It's all the time like this. I ask you one thing, and then you turn the answer the way that you wish. And that is how you gave us now the expert opinion, because the notion of the shield is to get a sword in the shield, rather than your body. So I showed you this photograph, and my specific question was because yesterday you told when asked by the Prosecutor that they were mixed with soldiers. That is what you told us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm asking you to show us on the photograph how is it that you moved toward those houses? So that is my question: How is it that you were walking towards those houses which we see in this picture here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were moving towards those houses together with soldiers who were in this group, who were eight or nine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Together, or mixed with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the first one. I was in front of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in a single file?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was the first one. We walked down the street, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I just need a point of clarification here because counsel is now referring to Dumpor house, and he is saying those are the houses which are depicted on this photograph. But that's not the case. These houses I don't think are Dumpor's houses. I really want a clarification on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think Judge Clark asked the same question concerning those houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm sorry. If we're talking at cross-purposes, then obviously it is my fault. It is all my responsibility. Because I have it in my head, and yet I am unable to tell you about it. The witness is telling us how they reached those houses, how they walked. And it doesn't really matter whether these are Dumpor's houses or some other houses. He is telling us about the human shield, my learned friend. I'm asking him how is it that he was moving towards those house. Very simple. And I don't understand what is the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You are confusing matters because you are saying actually the houses which are reflected in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Speak to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think my learned colleague is confusing the matters because he is referring to the houses on the photograph. That is his exact words, reading from the transcript. He says, "The Dumpor's houses, as reflected in the photograph on the ELMO." And that's not the case. It really confuses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, it's for the benefit of this Chamber for you to make it clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Her Honour Judge Clark asked me if those were Dumpor's houses, and we said that no, they were not and that they were a few hundred metres away from here. The witness explained that, and I did that, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Then why is counsel then saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bos. It doesn't harm anybody if you ask the question again and help us to clear up this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: -- bear in mind that this witness, without a doubt, was a prisoner for a while and that he must have been through some fairly harrowing experiences. Perhaps you don't accept the full extent of them, but he is still due respect as a witness who has been a victim. So maybe the tone can be a little more gentle, and then the responses will be less excited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour. I always bear that in mind. I've realised of late what is the problem. The problem is the difference of the language, and that we have to wait for the interpretation. Not only this witness or some other, I realise immediately when the witness is dodging the answer, and then I have to ask him again. And then the confusion arises, and then perhaps somebody thinks that I'm not being polite. But these are all reactions, and it never crossed my mind not to be polite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, my question is: Are these Dumpor's houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please use the pointer to show us where the Dumpor's houses are and how far, roughly, are they from this place. Perhaps we could change it; perhaps we could take the big photograph. Now, show us where these houses are and where Dumpor's houses are, and please do it with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is these houses which we saw a minute ago. And Dumpor's houses are roughly somewhere here, next to the -- these woods here, somewhere in this corner down here. So we took the road. Sometimes we would get away, move through the woods, and reached this power transmission installation. Then we proceeded here to the right to approximately fetching up somewhere near these houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So what we see on the edge of the photograph is a hill, or do you want me to give you another photograph? That's the hill above Rastani, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the end of the photograph. You see, from where the photograph was taken. Where the number is, you see this number down here on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a hill from which these shots are taken, and Rastani can be seen as if in the palm of your hand, as the saying goes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, show me, on this large photograph - if, that is, we can see it - how far did the BH army withdraw? No, let's start like this. According to you, what was -- how far did the BH army advance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in their attack when they took Rastani.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they were in Dumpor's houses that morning. In Dumpor's houses, they were soldiers of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did they withdraw? Can one see that place on these photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think -- well, I'm not sure if it is in my statement, but I saw them with my own eyes. From these houses, around from these houses towards the railroad tracks and down the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you use the pointer and show us where down the village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, more or less here, or perhaps this way. And so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And going where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were moving from one house to the other. But as you said, behind this hill, the village of Rastani can be seen as if in the palm of your hand. And as they transferred from one house to the other, they became targets as they moved from one house to the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the HVO knew exactly what houses they were in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, where did you -- will you bring this photograph down. Will you move it to the middle so that we can see Neretva. Bring it down slightly so that we can see the river, so we can see the Neretva. Yes, fine. Will you now please use the pointer and point at the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it's this here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, don't you think it's a bit further away? Let me help you. The lower one, don't you see here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what was the relevance. You could also point at the Neretva to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you if you know where it is. If you don't, tell me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said I thought it was this, the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the other bank of the river, whose positions, who held that bank of the Neretva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look down the Neretva on the right-hand side, the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were crossing the river, returning to their positions; is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the positions -- unfortunately, we do not have this photograph so the Chamber could gain a picture, and according to the last decision, as far as I understand, we shall not be going to see it personally. But so that the Chamber can gain the picture of what Rastani looks like and where whose position was. My apologies, Witness, my colleague warns me again. Because of the speed, the transcript does not say who mans the positions on the - now, how are we going to say - on the left or the right-hand side of the Neretva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left-hand side of the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the left-hand side of the Neretva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking downstream, on the left-hand side, these positioned were manned by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, will you please be so kind and use a dotted line to indicate the direction of your movement, what you pointed to us with a pointer a while ago? And then draw the line to show where the Neretva is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Neretva River, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really find my way to the Neretva here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, weren't you sent to Rastani after it was established from the hill that the BH army had taken to its heels and that everybody was leaving Rastani and was heading for the Neretva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could say that about me and my colleague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you about you, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the time we were sent down that hill, the soldiers who were down there - that is, those infantry units - had already entered the first house in Dumpor's village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you were sent down there, Witness, wasn't it established from the HVO positions that the BH army had abandoned the village of Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the positions of the BH army were on the 21st -- between the 21st of September and the 23rd of September? Do you have any idea where those positions were? Do you have any personal knowledge of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. But a soldier of the BH army was killed that day in the Dumpor -- in Dumpor's houses, perhaps in one of those first houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him being killed and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I only saw him dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then please don't speculate. I'm asking you -- I'm really begging you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you asked me, "If you were there." How could he be killed if those soldiers were not there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you a moment ago, Witness, and, well, don't think that this counsel doesn't understand how -- you're answering me what way and why you're answering me in this way. I'm asking you kindly, between the 21st of September and the 23rd of September. You said you didn't know personally, that you didn't know it of your own knowledge when this soldier was killed. He could have been killed on the 21st or the 23rd, but you don't know. You are making conjectures. And here it looks as if it were your personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it is time for a break because we need to focus and bring this cross-examination to an end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Remember that this witness told us in direct evidence that he came over one body and then another body and it was part of his task to move the bodies in. So this witness is able to comment on the nature of those bodies. Bear that in mind, because if you don't ask him, we'll ask him, were they fresh bodies?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, before we start, could you inform us how long you are going to take.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't think more than half an hour. It all depends on the witness, not on me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I really hope that we will be able to finish this witness today. This witness has been here for two weeks as of today. And because of last week, he has already been waiting for a long time. And I really hope that he finishes. If we don't finish him today, he has to come back on Tuesday, which is another four days. I hope that you can take that into account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. That's the very reason I asked how long Mr. Krsnik will take for this witness. You may proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let's try and conclude this as soon as possible. Let's try to concentrate and be specific. So let us try again, and I will ask you to answer as briefly as possible in order to clarify certain matters for the Trial Chamber. At what time in the morning of the 23rd of November --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, interpreter corrects: of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- did the clash break out when the HVO started fighting around Rastani. Please answer as briefly as you can and try to concentrate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The artillery attack began very early. I think it was between 5.00 and 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the infantry attack begin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A group of eight prisoners was taken at about 7:30 from the village of Djubrani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I didn't ask you about the prisoners. If you know when the infantry attack of the HVO began, please tell us. And leave aside the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to say that they were taken away at 7:30, and they had to go down to the village of Rastani on their own, and they were brought to the bunker to which I was brought by car. So when they got down to the village, they found the soldiers of Tuta's unit behind the houses, behind the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what time was it, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume they entered the first house between 11.00 and 12.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that the infantry attack by the HVO began at 7:30 and that they entered the first houses between 11.00 and 12.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And you were watching from a hill and saw the whole situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was allowed to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from the hilltop, you could see the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina retreating; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally saw several soldiers running across a field in the direction of the railway track.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time was it when the two of you set out for Rastani, and with what task did you set out, you and your friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember - and I didn't have a watch at the time - it could have been around maybe around 2.00 when we set out towards Rastani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were sent there to carry food, to bring food and refreshments, soft drinks and cigarettes, to the soldiers who were fighting, who were attacking the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the fighting was over because the soldiers were able to have lunch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell me, please - and show it on this photograph, if you can - did you go alone, the two of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which house did you find the soldiers, and where did you have lunch, if you can indicate that on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in Dumpor's houses, which are not visible on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is where you encountered the soldiers and where you had lunch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The group I found there was in the first house in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you certain that this was in Dumpor's houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember that you marked on the map the location, both for the Prosecution and for my learned friends yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, at the time, there was no one in Dumpor's houses, apart from the HVO soldiers, at 2.00 p.m. when you arrived there -- or excuse me, when did you arrive in Dumpor's houses? What time was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the trip there took about half an hour, maybe a little longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you arrived in Dumpor's houses after 2.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I may have set out at 1.30 p.m. I didn't have a watch, but it was around that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. How many dead HVO soldiers did you see and how many dead soldiers belonging to the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the road, we saw two dead soldiers belonging to the HVO, and afterwards, we had to collect the bodies of soldiers who had been killed on the other side of those houses. So I think that, all in all, there were seven HVO soldiers and one soldier of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did that after lunch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, the prisoners, have lunch together with the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This group of four, I think they did have lunch, and I think that the two of us did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't your primary task to come and collect the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, wasn't the reason why you were sent there precisely to collect the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my testimony, I told you what I did. I did what I was ordered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's exactly what I was asking you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first task we were given was to collect the bodies of those who had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, when you were in Dumpor's houses, did you hear that three prisoners killed -- slaughtered three HVO soldiers who had been wounded and then fled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Dumpor's houses?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Dumpor's houses, none of the seven soldiers were slaughtered, and I can assert that with certainty. Of the seven soldiers we carried there, not a single one had had his throat cut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are talking about HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, none of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the sake of the record, we are talking of the 23rd of September at about 2:30 p.m., which is when you first laid eyes on the HVO soldiers who had been killed. And you assert with certainty that not a single one had had his throat cut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of those seven.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And do you know that of those three prisoners -- that three of the prisoners fled, escaped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that only in November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you learn how they managed to escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were told to check whether there were any soldiers of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting you. Did you also learn the date when that happened? Was it the 22nd or the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they escaped?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were told to go into a house to see if there were any army soldiers inside. And when they entered the house, they really did find a group of soldiers belonging to the army. And they prevented them from going back where they had come from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers of the army prevented them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they left with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't think all this took place in one single house. I think that they had been given different tasks and that perhaps there were two or three houses involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any case, it was prisoners from this group of eight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that four of them were left now, or five; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this group of four, one went missing, and no trace has been found of him since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had lunch, you collected the dead. What time could it have Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts – Pages 6743 to 6755. been then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think perhaps, perhaps nearly 3.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you had lunch and gathered the dead all in half an hour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying this approximately. It could have been after 3.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And then you took the route that you marked on the picture. How many HVO soldiers were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my group?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember precisely how many, but let us say -- let's say there were around 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six of us prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Six. And how did you walk along this route that you marked? Did you go as a group, or did you march in file two by two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We walked in a group. We were all mixed together. Because if only we had gone in front and the soldiers behind, as you asked me a while ago, they would have been an easier target at that point, if there was a straggler from the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the side. So we and the soldiers from the unit were all mixed together in a group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take the pointer. You have drawn lines at a right angle. So can you use your pointer to make a square.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this corner here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no. Where the arrow is. You see where the line ends. Can you just -- not using a marker but the pointer, can you please trace a square toward the hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
