utterances.text: That's right, that's right. Excellent. So in this square, you see there is a wood, one house on one side, two on the other. Were there any B and H soldiers there? Couldn't you see from the hill that there weren't any left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, you're asking me questions as if I had taken part in planning and conducting this operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I understand. Tell us, please, couldn't the soldiers from the top of the hill who saw everything below -- it was already 3.00 p.m. Couldn't they see? Did they have Motorolas? Did they have communications?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So wasn't it obvious that there was not a single B and H army soldier left there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me put a counter-question to you. Why, then, did not the soldiers leave us behind and say, "You are prisoners and we shall go on and continue our operation"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, of course, I cannot answer your questions. But because some people escaped and you had to be guarded; isn't that logical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean we were sent into military action in order to be guarded there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another question: Did anyone shoot at you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there was sporadic gunfire but no major gunfire at that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any gunfire in this square?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That afternoon, you said that they could be seen running toward the Neretva. Were they -- had they gone a long way from the railway tracks by then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, let me tell you: The soldiers of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina had no communication among themselves, because they had no Motorolas or communications equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how those two men were taken prisoner. They didn't know where the other soldiers were. They didn't know that they were withdrawing, that some had already withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the soldiers who had been taken prisoner and who had no idea where the positions were at that exact moment or who they would encounter and where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw this. Did you talk to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that they did not have any communication with the soldiers they were supposed to meet up with in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they taken prisoner by your group or another group, those two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was not my group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they brought to you? Did you meet up somewhere along the road? Were they brought to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The soldiers used the Motorola to inform my group that they had taken two army of Bosnia and Herzegovina soldiers prisoner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did someone talk to them before you saw them? Were their Motorolas confiscated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know? Were you present when they were taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not present when they were taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, then. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me please, at 3.00 or 4.00 p.m., was not the village of Rastani completely in the hands of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please lower the photograph a little, just a little. Can we agree that where the arrow you have drawn is -- from that point to the River Neretva, there's a clear space?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there had been soldiers in these houses, they would have been found by 3.00 p.m. or they would have fired shots; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the arrow is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From these houses to the Neretva, can we agree now -- you see this little lake here at the top of the photograph. Do you recognise the River Neretva now? You can see a small pool or lake at the top of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So there's a clear place. And they would have had to leave a long time ago or they would have been shot like clay pigeons, either by the soldiers from the hilltop or those in the houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they could have been behind the railway track.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, is there a clear space between the railway track and the Neretva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see where the Neretva is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the railway track towards the top of the photograph, is that a clear space?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At 3.00 p.m., was there any shooting behind the railway track in the direction of the Neretva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was shooting all that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, please. It's 3.00 p.m., and you are near these houses. Were there soldiers running toward the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If they had been running, would you have seen them, or would they have been shot? Because there was a clear space. There was no cover.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they probably didn't dare take that route to retreat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then, am I not correct in saying that they all left long ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, then, no one fired shots at you? There were no soldiers in any of these houses, so what sort of human shield were you, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, half an hour ago I explained what a human shield is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. Now my next question, please: The petrol can that the soldier you called Splico had, how big was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a 20-litre canister, and he was carrying it in his hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How big was it? Can you describe it? Was it made of metal or plastic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't matter whether metal or plastic. Twenty litres is twenty litres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Where did he bring it from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he going into action carrying this petrol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed it when we left the house where we had had lunch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was carrying this on his own, and he set five to ten houses with twenty litres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did he have this kind of patch on his sleeve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, as for insignia, you can see in my testimony two days ago what I said about the insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. Very well. We know what you said. We have the transcript. That is why I put the statement to you, which you gave a long time ago when your memory was fresher. And you confirmed that what you told the investigators then was correct. Tell me, please, you don't remember the patch? If you're looking for it, it's on page 9, the first paragraph at the top of the page. We looked at it together where you describe the insignia of the Convicts Battalion. Tell me, do you know who liberated Rastani from whom in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You mean 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] No, 1992. I think there will be an objection, so I will explain its relevance right away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't the HVO and the army of B and H liberate Rastani from the JNA in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there not a lot of destruction in Rastani then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I said that in my statement, that almost every Serbian house - and they were in the majority in Rastani - was set alight in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that 70 to 80 per cent of these houses in the village were Serbian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what percentage it was, but I do know that more than half of the houses were Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Dumpor's houses were not Serbian houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you saw them, they were intact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. And tell us, so this Splico takes this can, goes around and ignites?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was it. And after that, nothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why? He ran out of petrol. Or didn't want to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think we have come down to those houses which probably were Serb, or I already said that this house that we were in had been damaged long ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Splico knows which houses are Serb and which are not Serb houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Serb houses were destroyed a year before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And no Muslim houses? Didn't the Yugo army shell Rastani? Wasn't that one of the principal battles for the liberation of Mostar in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If dozens and dozens of Bosniak houses in Rastani, what will it mean if I say yes, there were two or three or five of them destroyed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But Splico knows those which are intact, to Splico's mind, are Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Very well. And where does this Splico come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wouldn't Splico be a nickname for somebody from Split?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. You don't know. Very well. Tell me, please - and I'll try to be very clear, very short, and very to the point - you assume -- I mean, you assume that the old man called and those two men who had petrol poured over them to remain alive? You did not hear it on the Motorola, you personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I hear it over the Motorola?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So it is your assumption that the old man is Tuta; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now take your statement, page 11. Yes, yes, page 11 of your statement. Third passage, the last two sentences. And you say here very unambiguously, very unambiguously: "When he was" -- no. Let's do the whole sentence. "I think they survived only because when -- after being notified that those two were captured," now you say, "Tuta ordered to bring them alive." That is what you told The Hague investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But as a matter of fact, you don't know that, do you? Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I heard the soldier who told the others that he had received the order on the Motorola to bring them alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two days ago, you said "the old man," and you concluded. But today you said that you could not conclude that it was Tuta, you didn't hear Tuta, you didn't know it was Tuta. And I'm telling you - you see this is your statement in writing - you told The Hague investigators that it was Tuta. Did you say that to The Hague investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it doesn't change the context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Leave that to the Court. You are a witness. Don't be a witness, an expert witness, and the judge or the witness. You just tell us about what you know, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, my next question: Had those -- those two were taken to Siroki Brijeg, to a command - two days ago, you said "Tuta's command" - and that they were found there by the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Red Cross didn't find them there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, go one line below that and look at what you say in your statement. "That night we returned to the Heliodrom. Two captured detainees were taken to Tuta's house at Siroki Brijeg." Did you mean Tuta's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it is. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on. "They kept them in the cellar at Tuta's command in Siroki Brijeg. I heard it from a group of 15 to 20 detainees who were also kept secretly at Tuta's headquarters in Siroki Brijeg. This group was brought to Heliodrom later, and they told me the story. We were able to inform the ICRC about this, and the ICRC found those two in the basement of Tuta's headquarters." A second ago you said that you never said that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, counsel, sir, in my statement two days ago, I provided a sequence of events which is accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. But let me --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The International Committee of the Red Cross found them in Ljubuski when undoubtedly, undoubtedly, that organisation had put pressure or somebody else put pressure on the HVO, on Tuta's unit, or I don't know who, and they were transferred sometime between -- during the latter half of November to Ljubuski and registered there. And this could also be a mistake in interpretation at the time when I was making my statement. But I do not think that it is of the highest relevance for the two men who were captured and kept hidden for two months by Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. All right. Do you want me to let him go on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've finished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Very well. Witness, all that you told us is something that you heard. You have no personal knowledge about this, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I and a group of detainees --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, once again, I'm asking you if know this personally or did you hear about this? This is a simple answer, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard from the officials of the International Committee of the Red Cross the things that I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that you heard it from a group of 50 to 20 detainees. Shall we read it once again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Counsel, sir, from detainees, I heard they were being hidden in the cellar underneath Tuta's headquarters. And from the International Committee of the Red Cross, we heard that they had been found and registered between the middle and the end of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where? Where were they found and registered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure, but I think it was in the prison at Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Do you remember that two days ago they said they were not found?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could not find them -- they could not locate them for two months while Tuta hid them in the cellar underneath his headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "When he hid them." Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have personal knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in Tuta's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in Siroki Brijeg and saw Tuta hide them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My dear sir, with those soldiers, with those detainees, I was exchanged on the same day and at the same time of the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You heard it from others. Then don't tell us that you know it, if you heard it from others.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I heard it personally from those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If need be, they will probably tell us about it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, tell me, and it says that this statement was read out to you. It contains all that I said. It was read in Bosnian and translated. And then you said: "And we informed the Red Cross about it, and the Red Cross found those two men in the cellar of Tuta's headquarters." So that is not true, what you told the investigators.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dear, sir --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say that? Tell me first.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew it exactly then, and now, where they had been found. And I knew exactly where they had been hidden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please, did you say that to The Hague investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I'm repeating, perhaps it was a misinterpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go into private session, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are now in the open session. Mr. Par, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you very much, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness SS. My name is Zelimir Par, and I'm one of the counsel for Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you a few questions related to your testimony so far. I'd like to suggest that we start from that day, 6th and 7th of July, 1993. That is the day when you left Heliodrom to go to work for the unit for which you told us it was Stela's unit. You remember that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the outset, I'd like to ask you to look at a document and discuss those dates and that work. It is Prosecution Exhibit P434, from binder 19 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we have to wait for this document and look at it, I will tell the Chamber what we are talking about. This is an order to send prisoners of war to work. I am afraid there is no English version of this document, but it is very easy to understand, even in its original version, because these are all tables. At the same time, could we place it on the ELMO for the witness to see, because it's only a couple of sentences. Oh, you found it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: What book is it from, Mr. Par? Did you say "19" or "9"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nine, nine, nine. Binder 9. P434.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness SS, if you have this document before you, will you please have a look at it and tell us what it is about. And then I'll ask you a question. So tell me when you are ready. Let us only deal with the first page, so as not to waste too much time. So you can see it is a document entitled, "Order to assign prisoners of war to labour." Do you see the title of this document? We can -- can we see who issued this document? Can you see that it says: "Military secret, strictly confidential," the reference number? Can you see all that? And now, if you turn page 1, do you see that it says: "Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna, Ministry of Defence, Military Police Administration, Garrison 1711"? Can you see all that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, look at the dates, 6th and 7th of July, 1993. That is, it is the dates when you went out to work. And will you please look at what it says here. Because you can see that you have columns, order to assign people to work, a certain date, the reference number, and the person in charge, the person in charge of the prisoners of war being taken out to work assignment. Now, will you please look at the dates, 6th and 7th of July, 1993, from number 12, down to 20. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what I'd like to ask you -- we were talking about who took you out from Heliodrom that day. You mentioned that as far as you could remember, you were not quite sure but that it could have been somebody called Luka who was there. My question is: Could it be this Luka Barisic because it says here that on the 6th and 7th, he was the person in charge of taking persons out. Could it be that Luka Barisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what his last name was. But I'm not sure about his name at all. I believe I said I think his name was Luka. But there was also Luka who always took prisoners to the military police. And I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But we can confirm that Luka Barisic's name appears here, at least in this document, on the 6th and 7th of July, '93. You can see that, can't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, look at these dates, 6th and 7th. Which unit could it be that they were taken to? Can you see that? On the 6th and 7th, it was all the 1st Light Assault Brigade. Can you see that? Now, what I was about to ask you: Would you allow for that possibility, that on the 6th and 7th of July, you were taken by a soldier from the Light Assault Brigade, judging by this document, judging by the fact that this name Luka figures here? Would you grant that it is possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement and my testimony, I never once mentioned the words "light assault," so I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what I wanted to show to you. Because I wanted us to see that at that moment, when you came out of the Heliodrom, whether you knew who was taking you and where, to what unit. Was it something that you could know, that you had positive knowledge of, or was it merely guesswork?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, we were men who had been captured. We had no right to ask names or where we were going or why we were going where we were going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, we are still at those dates, that is, the 6th and 7th of July. So you've left the Heliodrom. Will you now look at this photograph. You already saw it during the direct examination, and I see you find your way around very well. It is 14.4. Now, Witness, you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the direct examination, you said that you knew where this zone of so-called Stela's unit was, that you knew that to the left and to the right there were some other units, but that you could not accurately say where the boundaries of individual zones were. Am I right in saying this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I would nevertheless like to ask you: You mentioned that the military police was on one side of this Health Centre. So I'm not asking you exactly for the boundaries of the zone, but will you put, say, "1" at the place where you are positive was held by the military police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So will you please, if you are sure that the military police was at some place, put "1." I'm not asking you to draw any boundaries between the zones.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Likewise, since you have this photograph in front of you, can you show us where some other unit was on the other side, if you know which unit? And you will tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let us have it on the ELMO. Will you please use the pointer so that we can all see -- so that we can all see where the military police was, for instance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building here, this building here is the building of the Aleksa Santic Secondary School. Behind that building here, next to this corner, I worked and made a bunker on the 2nd of August. So this building must have been held by the military police. And one of the bunkers was right next to the corner of the building here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, on the other side of the Health Centre, what other units? Will you please point at number 2. Where did you put number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm not quite sure. I put number 4 here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It doesn't matter. It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was the 4th Battalion here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Very well. Now, talking about the 4th Battalion, you mentioned that in that area, in the 4th Battalion's area on that day, on the 6th or on the 7th - I'm not sure - you were working at a bunker carrying sandbags. Can you show us where that bunker is on this photograph and which you think was in the area of the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not how I put it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I misunderstood you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you misunderstood me. I said -- I said this is Liskina Street. And behind this building, somewhere down to these houses here, we carried sandbags on the 7th of July. I carried them only. Some other soldiers were -- made a bunker here, somewhere here, between these houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Will you keep the pointer there, please, just keep the pointer there. Now, according to you, in your view, is that the zone of Stela's unit or of the 4th Battalion? Do you know that, or did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, Stela's soldiers were with us. They had brought us from in front of his headquarters and guarded us there the whole day. So that I assume that a bunker that we made was used by his unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I suppose I understand you well. You are saying this only because there were soldiers with you, but you have no positive knowledge of where the 4th unit's zone began and where Stela's unit ended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could not see the plan of assignments or the combat orders of the units to give an accurate answer. I'm telling you only what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that is what I'm trying to show here. That even if you came there with Stela's units, it is still nevertheless possible that you worked both for Stela's and for the 4th Battalion, if it had to do with the fortification of bunkers or something like that. And that is all that I wanted to achieve by asking you these questions. But let me also make use of your excellent memory to help us with it -- to help us with something, if you can. We have asked a number of witnesses to draw it on this photograph. Do you remember if, on -- when -- where on the street which you called Liskina Street, where were those sandbags? Could you draw them here, to the best of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Unfortunately, I still take this -- walk this street very often, and to within 30 metres or even more. I'm not sure where those sandbags were, because when I walk this street, I look at this, I look for this wall, and I look for that. I'm not sure. And I take this street very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But could you take the pointer, point at those 30 metres roughly, where they were approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my guess would be here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you mark it. And perhaps say that it could be plus, minus 30 metres. So put just a small question mark next to that line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very good. Now, do you remember perhaps, if there -- if beyond these sandbags, up this street, there was a cord from this -- hanging from this Health Centre, which -- over which some blankets or some sheets or something were hung as a screen, as a kind of protection from the gunfire, from the sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only saw it between the Hotel Ero and the post office, nowhere else. There, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if we are talking about the Health Centre, do you remember how many entrances the Health Centre had at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if there was one entrance next to this fountain? Do you remember if you could enter the Health Centre from there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never passed from the -- by the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could we go into private session very briefly? I have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us recall the event in connection with the flat in Kajtaz over the taking out of the things in the flat. You said, as far as I remember, that a family was probably evicted from that flat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to establish whether you knew the Kajtaz family.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what happened to the family, or do you only assume what happened? I'm talking about that particular family.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is not hard to guess what happened to the Kajtaz family when we entered the flat, which was intact, and the family was missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that you are coming to conclusions based on your way of thinking. I am simply trying to establish whether this is your conclusion or whether you had any definite information. I can see now from your response that this is your conclusion on the basis of your knowledge. But you do not have any information about this, about where they went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have finished with that flat and the things in it, so I have only a few more questions for you. At one point, you mentioned that Stela's unit was called Mrmak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the insignia of this unit, or just the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I never said anything about insignia. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. If you would bear with me. I have just one more question. When you were taken to work, you were taken to Balinovac, among other places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A mosque was destroyed there. Do you know who did that, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard on the first or second day I was there, while I was working there, from the soldiers who were guarding us -- and they were members of the military police. I heard from them -- or rather, I heard them talking among themselves saying that the mosque had been destroyed by an old man called Misic, or he had given the orders for it to be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I have no further questions. Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'm hearing the B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. There must be some problems with the channels. Can you try it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes. It must be fine now. Re-examined by Mr. Bos:

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I just have a couple of things. I would like the witness to be shown, again, Exhibit 34.2, which is the map of Rastani which he marked himself. And I would like also to have the long photograph, which I think is 34.3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, what I would like you to do is you've -- in cross-examination, you've been examining this long photograph. And what I would like to do is that you would mark on this map the area which we can see on this long photograph so it's very clear to the Judges which part of the map we actually -- is depicted on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could you put the photograph on the overhead projector, please, especially the left part where he marked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What we see here, could you please circle on the map, put a circle where that is on the map, what we see on the screen. So that part which you have actually marked, if you can circle that on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this map with a circle?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe what you could do is put a circle where you think on the map is this electricity complex.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you also, please, mark for us where you think that photograph was taken. Put an arrow from where -- on the map the position where that photograph was taken from so that we know from which side the photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that it would be fair to the witness, and to us, to have Dumpor's houses marked and Neretva as well. Because now I am confused, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: To be honest, I'm a bit confused as well as to where the arrow was placed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you look again at the map. And are you absolutely sure that the photograph -- I know it's very complicated. Are you absolutely sure that the photograph which we now see on the ELMO was taken from the point where you placed the arrow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a topographical map of the kind used in war. It's not a picture. It wasn't taken from one side or another. I put the arrow here looking at Rastani in the direction of the hill approximately. So this arrow shows how it is seen from the side controlled by the army of BH. So Dumpor's houses would be where number "2" is. And as I said, we went from Dumpor's houses to Elektroprenos here. Then we turned right, but we didn't go far. And we stopped at some houses there. When we were there at those houses, information was received that two soldiers had been taken prisoner, and we were told to go with the other soldiers left from the road we had come by, and we found the imprisoned soldiers with a group of soldiers in houses here approximately. So this crossroads here is, in fact, this angle here, which I drew on this picture, this photograph. And Elektroprenos is here, which I have marked here in front of this crossroads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe it this way: Would it not be that the photograph was actually taken from the spot on the top of the map, rather than on the bottom where you've put the arrow, if you look at the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph was taken from the direction from which the HVO army came, which is from this direction up here, from the top of the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you, then, please mark the spot where you think the photographer was. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this photograph?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That photograph. Where would he have been on the map? Not on the photograph, but on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows clearly, in my mind -- or rather, this map is a map of the village of Rastani, which can be seen from the other side of the Neretva. So the photographer, if this were the photograph, would have been able to see the village the way it looks approximately, perhaps from the area of Vrapcici or something like that, which is on the other bank of the Neretva, as I marked it with an arrow. Let me just tell you, sir, on this photograph, you cannot see Dumpor's houses, which we can see here on this picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, looking at the photograph, where would Dumpor's houses be? I know it's not on the photograph, but where would it be? In which direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would be here, in this corner somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you can circle that corner, if you don't mind, or -- well, I know it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. You can draw on my exhibit. I allow you to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Maybe because -- I don't know if it's clear, we can show a video of Rastani, and maybe the witness will then be able to identify the Dumpor's houses on the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I don't have any objections. I don't know the reasons. [Interpretation] I don't know what the purpose or the relevance of this is. We showed it on the photograph. We showed it on the map. What's the use of showing it on the video? I simply don't see the relevance of showing it on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: The relevance, Your Honour, is we still haven't seen the houses. We don't have a photograph of it. We've only seen it on the map. And it may be on the video. I must say it may be. I'm not sure if the witness will be able to identify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How long will that video last?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you allow me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I do have an objection, Your Honour, because, again - and I do strenuously object - because attempts are being made again to show houses that have been burnt down, houses that have been destroyed. We do not know when or who did this because Rastani was taken five times. There was a big clash in 1992 with heavy artillery. And when Your Honours see these images, this will leave the impression -- well, I don't know what it has to do with my client, the total picture, the total image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, from the maps and from the photographs, we have got a rough idea of the situation there already. And if you want to show some videotapes, you had better do it in your direct examination, rather than the cross -- re-examination at this stage. So Mr. Bos, our advice is that you withdraw this request.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, yes. I think we are entitled to show the video, but if the Judges think that it will not be helpful to them, I'm not insisting. So I'll leave it in your hands. If you prefer not to see the video, then that's the end of my redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from the Judges? Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes, I have a number of questions, and I hope I don't keep everybody too late. Witness SS, you were talking about how, when you went to the Heliodrom, that you were given old JNA air force overalls that were blue, and that led to your group collectively being known as the Blue Orchestra. Do you remember how long you had these blue uniforms before you were taken to Stela's headquarters - for the moment, I'll say that - on what you think was on the 6th or the 7th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I wore the blue uniform approximately until the first day when I was in Stela's unit. On that day, while we were taking the things out of the flat, I took a T-shirt for myself - it had no sleeves - and an old track suit, the lower part, the trousers of a track suit. So I managed to change out of my blue uniform, which caused trouble for me every day. Some people wore the blue uniform throughout the summer. But I have to emphasise I don't know if they had chosen small sizes on purpose or whether they really were all small in size, but these uniforms, for a man of my size -- they were for a man of my size, but they also had to be worn by men who were much taller, who were a metre and 95, a metre point 95 taller, and a hundred kilograms in weight. And this degraded them, this humiliated them even more because they looked so miserable in those uniforms that were too small for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sir, as I understand it, by your own efforts, you managed to avoid wearing that blue uniform from the first day that you went to Stela's unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 6th of July, I no longer wore the uniform, and maybe a few other people managed to avoid wearing them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: When you gave your testimony two days ago, you described how when you were brought to a certain premises in the town of Mostar, that some of the soldiers said, "Boss, these are the men from the army," and you had your first encounter with Mr. Stela. Were most of you in the blue uniform on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That morning, when we arrived at Stela's unit, I believe we all wore blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And I have a recollection that you described how Mr. Stela said to you, "Do you think you're here by accident?" Did he explain the reason why you were there? Did he talk further to you after he said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I described it in my statement at great length. Well, when he came --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'll just repeat that because I cut across you. Sorry. We don't ever see your statement, so you have to help us with that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the men who drove us to Stela's headquarters said that we should wait there for the boss. And in about 15 minutes, a red Jeep appeared, and from it, a man stepped down. And by the reaction, both of the soldiers and his own reaction, we assumed it was Stela. The men who brought us there told him, "Boss, these are the ones from the BH army." And he started yelling, cursing, threatening and told us to stand against a wall, put our heads down, and then proceeded to beat a man that we talked about a while ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes. But did he ever explain to you what he meant by, or did you appreciate what he meant by the statement "Do you think you're here by accident"? Did you understand that to mean something specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I'm concerned, I took it to mean - and others, too - that his unit had asked for us, specifically for the 25 of us to be brought there that very day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. You also described that when you arrived at this premises, that it appeared from the inference that you draw from the state of the premises and the name of the family on the door to have been recently vacated. And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: -- and can we, the Court, take it from that that it was one of the first days that Mr. Stela was going into occupation of this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can do is make guesses, make assumptions. But it is 100 percent certain that that family had been evicted from their apartment two, three, or five days before that, just as -- just like thousands of other families.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, I know that you spent many days on different parts of the front line. I don't know if you ever went back to that house that had been recently evacuated. But if you can, could you describe to us what the building was like. I don't need very fine detail, but was it a villa or an apartment house or a very modern block, or what sort of premises was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, I spent three days in front of that building; that is, I was there on three occasions. And I think that that building had two floors only. And I remember that this flat was on the second floor of that building, that that is where the headquarters was, where I went from which we had to take out those things, where I cleaned weapons --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, you described a little later how you heard that the unit that Stela commanded was called Mrmak and that you heard something about a dog, this being the name of his dog. Who did you hear that from and approximately - I don't need the dates - but approximately when did you hear that? Was it before or after you went to this recently vacated apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the first day that I was there, I saw "Mrmak" written on a car. And at that moment, it looked a bit odd to me. But people who knew about that explained it that day after we returned to the camp, and so on and so forth, that that was the name of Stela's dog. But whatever, the cars said "Mrmak."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: When you were leaving the camp in the morning to go out and do certain work, were you ever told by anyone at the camp or when you were on the way to wherever you were being taken, were you ever told who had requested your presence to do work and where you were going?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I must say one thing: In the HVO army, there were hundreds of soldiers who fought, who waged war honourably. There were hundreds of soldiers who behaved honourably and protected the dignity of prisoners. And by doing that, they were also protecting their own dignity, the dignity of their street, of their town, of their people, and so on and so forth. However, that does not apply to the two men we are talking about here in this case, in this trial. When a car turns up to take people to Stela's unit and when another, a blue car, turns up to take people to the military police, the camp inmates would practically suffer cardiac infarctions. It is not simple to explain it in this relaxed atmosphere. It is impossible to -- I mean, the horror beggars description. A guy, a good friend of mine, suffered a nervous breakdown when in the human shield at Rastani. He is in a psychiatric sanitorium to this day. That young man who went missing in Rastani in September 1993, his mother, she lives alone, she has nobody. Until last year, she could not come to terms with the fact that her son was dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I can understand that. I don't want to cause you any pain. You can take it that for my part - I can only speak for me - that I do understand that everybody suffers appallingly in war and especially when, as you describe, these are your own people. I just want to ask you a few more questions because I'm very conscious of the fact that I'm using up valuable time. Yes, and I'm reminded of that. I had some notes of what I wanted to ask. Yes. Just two more questions. I think you've answered one already. When you were in Rastani, and being used as you described, were any of you wearing your blue air force uniforms at that stage, or how were you dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody had the blue uniform in Rastani. Everybody had somehow tried to manage in the course of the summer to replace the uniform by something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Do you recall how were you dressed in comparison with the soldiers who were guarding you or who were engaged in combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot remember what I was wearing in Rastani. But those were basically some thin -- some light T-shirts, some old sportswear, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The point was just to see whether you were dressed as soldiers. And the final question I want to ask you is: When you came across first one body as you were going down with the lunch to the soldiers in the first house, and then another body, and then you talked about five other bodies behind the house, and a body from the ABiH, can you tell me the condition of those bodies? Were they from a previous encounter, or what was their condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The bodies of those killed soldiers were in a condition that allowed one to establish easily that they had been killed only a few hours or a few minutes earlier. Some were bloody. The two bodies which I came across, walking towards the village, may have been killed perhaps a few hours earlier, several hours earlier. Those men were lying there. There were very many insects covering their eyes and all that, and the rigor mortis had, I believe, started to set in. I'd really rather not talk about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I didn't want you to go into that kind of detail. Thank you very much for your assistance. I'm sorry to have opened old wounds for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's questions? Yes, Mr. Par, maybe you could be the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Very briefly. Further cross-examination by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, who gave you those uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was those guards, the police, at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any criteria where they singled some of you out and said some will have blue uniforms, others will not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They provided those uniforms for us because we were 25 or 27 -- I can't remember exactly. But those uniforms were given only to us who had been captured as members of the army Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you subsequently check whether you were wearing those uniforms? Did somebody take care of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, since you say they were all small sizes, and it was humiliating to wear them, do you know if it was an army secondary school before the war, that they had cadets, boys 15 to 17, who were wearing those uniforms? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that. But it was quite possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Further cross-examination by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 21st of September, did the BH army attack and take Rastani over from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the judge, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is because of the Dumpor's houses and the bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't the 21st. The Armija put Rastani under it's control, if my memory serves me well, on the 19th of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excellent, on the 19th of September. Could it be possible -- of course, I know that you do not know it, but could it be possible that men were killed then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were people killed on that occasion, too, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, I do not have any further questions. You do not have to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I do not have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much, Witness, for helping us. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of the room. Yes, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I do have a few exhibits to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If I can do that now, I would like to tender Exhibit 20.8 as marked. That's the photograph of the HV barracks in the Heliodrom. Slash 3, all right. Then that's a new exhibit, Exhibit 34.10, which is the map of the Rastani area, the big map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And then 34.10/1 as the map as it was marked. And Exhibit 890, which is the sketch of the patch. And Exhibit 34.2/1, which is the smaller map as marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess there's no objections from the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I also have some exhibits to tender, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we have no objections. But we would like to tender certain documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: All those documents are admitted into the evidence. Yes, you may continue, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies to you, Your Honour. So counsel for Mr. Martinovic proposes P434, which is this order to send people for work out of the camp, and the map 14.4 with markings made by the witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D1/38. It was the Exhibit 20.8, and D1/31. It was Exhibit 34.3. I'd like to tender them into evidence as Defence exhibits. Those are the photographs, you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So those documents have been admitted into the evidence. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise for taking one more minute of the Chamber's time. Just some schedule questions. Apparently there's some schedules floating around the building showing you to be sitting on another matter next week in the afternoons, which is the same time that we're sitting. And we don't know if there's any confusion about that. This case is sitting in the afternoons next week from approximately 2.00 to 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You mean next Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I mean next week in general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Then there's a second question: There has also been an indication that Mr. Milosevic will be appearing in the Court again on the 11th of December. In the past, it has been the case - I don't know why - but we can't seem to do any other business in this building when he is here. Are we to understand it that we will not be in session on the 11th of December?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Here I also have an announcement to make concerning the sittings of next Monday. Because of the technical problems, we'll start our hearing at 5.00 p.m. Monday afternoon instead of 4.30, which means we'll have a night session. During that sitting, we will somehow relax the rules in this courtroom; that is, the refreshments will be allowed in this courtroom so long as we can keep this room clean. Another matter is, as the Prosecutor mentioned just now, there will be no sitting on 11th of December, which means during that week, we only have one day; that is the Monday. The third matter is that this room will be used for another case, so we would like to ask everybody to take out all the personal belongings and the documents out of this room. We'll adjourn until next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
